title: Celebrate Kitchener's Urban Forest at the First Forestry Fall Fair
content: Residents of all ages are invited to explore the city's urban forest at Kitchener's first Forestry Fall Fair on Saturday, September 26 from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Huron Natural Area.

The event will feature crafts and family-friendly activities, face painting, self-guided nature walks and opportunities to discover the important role trees and natural areas play in creating a healthy, sustainable community.

City of Kitchener staff from Forestry and Natural Areas, Stormwater and Sanitary Utilities, and the Neighbourhood Development Office will be joined by representatives of local community organizations including REEP Green Solutions, the Region of Waterloo, Grand River Conservation Authority, Kitchener Nature Stewards and Bird-friendly Kitchener to provide more in-depth information to visitors.
Whether you're a nature enthusiast, a curious learner or looking for a fun family outing, the Forestry Fall Fair offers something for everyone.
For more information, visit Kitchener.ca/ForestryFair

title: Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park opens November 14, expanding sport, recreation and active living access for a community in motion
content: The City of Kitchener will officially open the new Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park on Saturday, November 14, creating more opportunities for residents of all ages and abilities to connect, compete, and belong through sport, recreation and community experiences. Community members are invited to join the grand opening ceremony and stay for family-focused activities throughout the day.   As the largest capital project in the City’s history, the centre is designed to respond to the needs of a growing and changing community by expanding access to indoor sport and recreation opportunities, while creating a welcoming place for people to get active, spend time together and build connections with others. Located in RBJ Schlegel Park, the centre is expected to bring the community together with more than 500,000 visits in the first year alone, and provide additional training, practice and competition space for dozens of local sport organizations.

"The opening of Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park is one of the most significant investments in community infrastructure in Kitchener's history," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "This facility will help more children learn to swim, give families more opportunities to be active together, provide welcoming spaces for residents of all abilities, and bring people together through sport, recreation and community events."

The centre includes a quad gymnasium, FIFA-sized indoor turf field that can be divided into four playing areas, two cricket practice nets, competition and leisure pools, and an indoor walking track. Together, these spaces will support a wide variety of sports like basketball, volleyball, soccer, lacrosse, cricket, futsal, pickleball, badminton and swimming.   For local sport organizations, this additional space will create opportunities to expand programs, accommodate more participants and help reduce waitlists. For residents, it means more chances to discover a new activity, or to continue playing a sport they already enjoy.   “We’re incredibly excited to welcome the community into the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park,” said Michael May, Deputy Chief Administrative Officer for the City of Kitchener. "From the very beginning, this facility has been designed with the people who will use it most top of mind: players, families, fans, coaches, partners and volunteers. Whether someone is attending their first swim lesson, playing in a basketball tournament, walking the indoor track or cheering on a family member, we want their experience to be welcoming, accessible and enjoyable."
More than a sports facility, the Cowan Recreation Centre is designed as a community gathering space that will create lasting benefits for the entire community:

More opportunities to stay active – The Cowan Recreation Centre expands Kitchener's indoor recreation options, providing more diverse opportunities for residents to participate in more sport, recreation and physical activity opportunities year-round.

Accessible for everyone  – Designed to meet the highest standards of any City facility, the centre features ramp access to both pools, wider pathways, guiding floor textures and accessible viewing areas, making it easier for people of all ages and abilities to participate, watch and connect with others.

Built for sustainability  – As the City's first net-zero carbon building and one of Canada's most sustainable municipally owned recreation facilities, the centre includes rooftop solar power generation, geothermal energy, mass timber construction, stainless steel pools, stormwater management and a green roof.

A venue for major events – Built to host provincial and national competitions, tournaments and events, the centre will showcase Kitchener, support local businesses and generate millions of dollars in economic activity, while giving local athletes the opportunity to compete closer to home.

On November 14, residents are invited to celebrate the official opening of the Cowan Recreation Centre, located in the heart of RBJ Schlegel Park (1664 Huron Road). Beginning at 9 a.m. , the free community event will feature something for all ages, including an official ribbon-cutting ceremony, guided tours of the facility, free public swims and sport activities, family-friendly entertainment including bouncy castles and face painters, equipment demonstrations, giveaways, prizes and activities throughout the day. The day's programming schedule will be published closer to the event.

To stay up-to-date on grand opening details, future programming and amenities, and more, visit the City's newly launched RBJ Schlegel Park webpage which includes detailed information about the Cowan Recreation Centre – Kitchener.ca/RBJSchlegelPark
For more information:
Corporate Communications and Marketing  City of Kitchener  Media@kitchener.ca

title: Celebrate a season of gardening, growth and community at Kitchener in Bloom's end-of-season celebration
content: From colourful flower beds and thriving vegetable gardens to pollinator-friendly spaces, Kitchener residents have spent the growing season helping neighbourhoods bloom. Now, the community is invited to come together and celebrate those efforts at the City of Kitchener's Kitchener in Bloom End-of-Season Celebration.

Taking place on Thursday, September 24, from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. at the Victoria Park Pavilion , this free community event will bring together gardeners, families and green space enthusiasts from across the city to connect, learn and celebrate another successful growing season.

Participants will have the opportunity to chat with local gardening organizations, listen to educational talks with horticultural experts, connect with other gardeners, enjoy family-friendly activities and enter prize draws. Light refreshments will also be available.

Kitchener in Bloom recognizes the important role residents play in beautifying neighbourhoods, supporting biodiversity and creating vibrant, welcoming green spaces throughout the city. Whether tending to a backyard garden, growing vegetables, planting native species or caring for a community garden plot, residents help make Kitchener a greener and more sustainable city.

The end-of-season celebration offers an opportunity to recognize these contributions while bringing together gardeners of all experience levels to share ideas, learn from one another and find inspiration for future growing seasons.
Residents are encouraged to reserve their spot in advance by registering through Eventbrite .
To learn more about Kitchener in Bloom and other neighbourhood greening initiatives, visit LoveMyHood.ca/bloom .

title: Eight-Week Program Helps Entrepreneurs Build Stronger Businesses
content: Entrepreneurs looking to start, grow, or acquire a business are encouraged to apply to Starter Company Plus, an intensive eight-week program designed to help participants ages 18 and older build the skills and confidence needed to move their business forward.

Delivered by the  Waterloo Region Small Business Centre in partnership with the Province of Ontario, Starter Company Plus is designed to address local economic development needs and provide support to entrepreneurs at all stages of their business journey.

Through expert-led training, personalized mentorship, and hands-on business planning, participants will learn how to build or strengthen their business plan, develop marketing, sales, operations, and financial skills, and refine their business pitch.

At the end of the program, participants will submit their business plan and pitch their business idea to a grant committee of local business professionals and private-sector stakeholders for the opportunity to secure a grant of up to $5,000.
Applications close on September 17, 2026, at 11:59 p.m .
To learn more, check eligibility and to apply, visit the Waterloo Region Small Business Centre website.

title: Statement by Kitchener Mayor Berry Vrbanovic on the 25th Anniversary of 9/11
content: Twenty-five years ago today, our world changed forever as we saw both the worst and the best of humanity.

On September 11, 2001,  one of the darkest days in modern history,  more than 3,000 innocent people , including several Canadians, left their homes, kissed their families goodbye, and began what they believed would be an ordinary day.
They never came home.

Among them were 343 New York City firefighters - 60 New York and Port Authority police officers, 8  paramedics,  a K9 unit – women and men,  who, when confronted with unimaginable danger, did something extraordinary.
They ran toward it.
Today,  Kitchener  remembers and  here at our Kitchener Firefighters Memorial, we remember them. All of them.
We remember their courage.  We remember their sacrifice.  And we remember the families who have carried their absence for twenty-five years.
But on this anniversary, we also remember what happened after the towers fell.
The world responded - not only with grief, but with humanity.
Kitchener firefighters travelled to New York to support the recovery efforts at Ground Zero, standing shoulder-to-shoulder with their American brothers and sisters.
Former Waterloo Mayor Dave Jaworsky delivered Blackberrys while in  a previous role, to be used in recovery efforts by the City and others.

Across Canada,  Canadians  responded with love and compassion as they opened their hearts and their homes as part of Operation Yellow Ribbon, which saw more than 33,000 passengers from over 225 flights land in 17 Canadian airports.

Nowhere  was that more  evident than in Gander,  Newfoundland, where almost 7,000 frightened strangers arriv ed  on diverted  aircraft, the folks who Came  From Away, and were welcomed, fed, sheltered and comforted for several days.
For those few remarkable days, there were no strangers. Decency and humanity prevailed.
There were simply people who needed help - and Canadians who were willing to give it.
That same spirit has defined the relationship between Canada and the United States for generations.
We are more than two countries sharing the  longest peaceful border in the world.
We are friends.  We are neighbours.  We are allies.
We have stood  together,  beside one another through wars,  tragedies and moments of profound uncertainty.

And at a time when our relationship  is fac ing unprecedented strains, perhaps this anniversary should remind us , especially the current US Administration, not only of where we have been - but of where we need to find our way back to.
Because twenty-five years later, the enduring lesson of September 11 cannot simply be about what hatred destroyed.
It must also be about what love rebuilt.
In a world that once again feels increasingly angry,  divided and conflicted, may we have the courage to choose another path.
Kindness over cruelty.
Understanding over division.
Peace over conflict.
Love over hate.
And when someone needs us - whether they live next door, across a border, or across an ocean - may we once again simply ask:
How can we help?
May we also choose kindness, may we always hug those closest to us a little tighter, and may we call the people we love more often, because as that day showed – tomorrow is never promised.
That, my friends, is how we honour those we lost.
And that is how we honour those  first responders  who ran toward danger,  not only on  that day,  but on  every  day they go to work to serve our communities .
That friends, is how we build the kind of peaceful and compassionate world they deserved.
Twenty-five years later, Kitchener and Canada remember.
Twenty-five years later, we still stand together.
And 25 years later, we commit again, we will never forget.

title: City of Kitchener presents September's Virtual LoveMyHood Grant Writing Workshop
content: Do you have an idea for a neighbourhood project that will bring people together? Looking for support to help make it happen?

The City of Kitchener's LoveMyHood Matching Grant helps residents turn their ideas into reality by providing funding for resident-led projects and neighbourhood initiatives. Ideas like street parties, little libraries, community art or neighbourhood greening, residents take the lead to create more connection in their neighbourhoods, and the City provides support along the way!
If you're interested in applying for a LoveMyHood Matching Grant but aren't sure where to start, join us for a free grant writing workshop and learn how to build a strong application.
Free Grant Writing Workshop
(Registration required)

Whether you already have a project idea or are just interested in learning more about the LoveMyHood Matching Grant, this interactive session will guide you through the application process, share tips for success and provide an opportunity to ask questions.
Register through Eventbrite or email lovemyhood@kitchener.ca for more information.
LoveMyHood Matching Grant applications are due on October 29, 2026.
Interested in applying, but can't make the workshop? Email lovemyhood@kitchener.ca to be paired with a Project Coordinator to support you through the grant process.
Visit LoveMyHood.ca/LMHGrant to learn more about the program, explore previously funded projects and start planning your application.
For more information: Marketing & Communications Associate Media@kitchener.ca

title: Discover, explore and learn at the Kitchener Fire open house
content: Kitchener Fire will open its doors to the community on Saturday, September 19 for its annual open house. From 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., residents can visit Kitchener Fire Headquarters at 270 Strasburg Road to learn about fire safety and the work of Kitchener Fire.

During the event, visitors can explore fire trucks and equipment, watch fire demonstrations, take part in interactive firefighting activities, meet mascot Sparky and his new friend Sniffy, jump in bouncy castles, have their faces painted, test their skills in the obstacle course and more. Don’t forget to fill out the event bingo card for a chance to win some free prizes.
The Lions Club of Kitchener will be hosting a BBQ and food trucks will be on-site with summer treats.
Admission is free but attendees are encouraged to bring non-perishable food donations in support of Food4Kids Waterloo Region.
For more information, visit Kitchener.ca/FireOpenHouse

title: Caring for our urban forest starts with good data
content: The City of Kitchener’s Forestry team is currently working in designated neighbourhoods to gather data for the 2027 block pruning program, as part of our Sustainable Urban Forest Strategy . Neighbourhoods are visited in rotation every seven to ten years to have blocks, or sections, of street trees pruned by arborists.

To plan and prepare for our 2027 block pruning, forestry staff are currently conducting tree inventory work in neighbourhoods, which includes gathering detailed information about each tree and taking photos of the trees with mobile devices.
The neighbourhoods scheduled for tree inventory work this fall include:
·  Bridgeport East
·  City Commercial Core
·  Fairfield
·  Pioneer Tower East
·  Pioneer Tower West
·  Rosenberg
·  Trussler
·  Westmount
When you see City staff in your neighbourhood, please treat them with respect as they work to care for our urban forest.
For more information and to view the full pruning schedule, visit Kitchener.ca/UrbanForestMap.

title: Help make back to school season safe in Kitchener
content: On September 8, schools across Kitchener will welcome new and returning students to their classrooms. With increased traffic during drop-off and pick-up times, we ask that you leave extra time when travelling and stay aware to help make this a safe back to school season for all.

The new Notre Dame Catholic Secondary School at 20 Woolner Trail is open for the 2026/27 school year, which means there are new road rules in and around the school zone. Pay attention to and comply with new speed limits, no stopping zones and school bus loading zones in this neighbourhood. Bylaw enforcement will be in effect.

There is a new crossing guard location at Fairway Road and Woolner Trail in addition to established crossing guard locations across the city. Visit the pedestrians and sidewalks webpage for a full list of crossing guard times and locations.
To help keep students, parents and road users safe, remember these tips to help make the start of school safer for everyone:
The City of Kitchener is committed to eliminating serious injuries and death due to traffic collisions in our community. Visit our Vision Zero page to find out more.
